articles.title: First launch
articles.summary: Start manually or configure optional AI providers.
steps: Choose New Project to see every supported starting path.
Manual editing and Manual Guided work without an AI provider.
Open Settings only if you want to configure Text, Vision or Image generation.
Use Quick Actions from the sidebar or Ctrl+K to find commands by name.
notes: Character Card Forge does not contact an AI provider until you explicitly request an AI action.

articles.title: Set up AI providers
articles.summary: Configure Text, Vision and Image roles independently.
steps: Open Settings and configure a Primary Text profile for character writing.
Assign Fast Text or Deep Review only when you want a different profile for those tasks; Use Primary is the default.
Configure Vision separately for image analysis and Image Generation separately for artwork.
Use each profile's connection or discovery controls before starting important work.
notes: Fallback is optional and should use a distinct profile. It handles bounded technical failures, not refusals or invalid content.
API keys stay in local app settings and are omitted from support reports and exported cards.

articles.title: Create your first character
articles.summary: Choose a creation route, review the draft and export deliberately.
steps: Choose New Project and select Blank Workspace, Manual Guided, Idea Generator, Character Collaborator, Idea Notebook or Template Start.
Select the starting template and confirm Create Project.
For AI routes, review proposed content before accepting it into the editable Workspace.
Check Description, Personality, Scenario and First Message, then save the project.
Add or generate artwork before PNG export when you want a visual card.
notes: Filling in Generation Concept alone does not create the finished character fields. Run Generate Character and review the result first.

articles.title: Import an existing character
articles.summary: Preview supported card or project files before copying, merging or replacing.
steps: Choose New Project, select Import Card or Project and confirm.
Select a supported Character Card PNG/APNG/JSON or Character Card Forge project package.
Review the detected format, portrait, validation, duplicate evidence and loss mapping.
Choose Copy, Merge or Replace only after the preview matches your intent.
notes: Merge and Replace retain recovery information where the workflow supports it; they are never automatic.

articles.title: Edit, inspect and improve a character
articles.summary: Use the Workspace, Card Inspector, AI Review and Revision History safely.
steps: Edit canonical fields directly in the Workspace and save meaningful progress.
Use Card Inspector for deterministic health checks, token estimates and export-facing metadata.
Run AI Review only when wanted; inspect every finding and proposed replacement.
Approve fields selectively. Rejected changes remain rejected and the accepted batch creates a recovery checkpoint.
Use Revision History to compare, restore, fork or selectively recover earlier values.
notes: AI scores are advisory, not objective measures of character quality.

articles.title: Find and organise characters
articles.summary: Search, filter, group and resize the Character Library.
steps: Open Character Library and search across projects, characters, card text and metadata.
Use workflow, review, token, Front Porch, privacy and deployment filters to narrow results.
Assign series, tags, folders and collections from Project Tools or batch actions.
Use Panels to collapse Filters, Project Tools or Details, and adjust card density for the available space.
Archive recoverably instead of deleting work you may need later.
notes: Portable/shared-folder libraries use a documented single-writer model; they are not automatic cloud sync.

articles.title: Create and manage artwork
articles.summary: Compose creative intent separately from provider execution settings.
steps: Open Image Studio and choose the active project and character.
Write or generate a character-aware prompt, then apply creative style controls or a reusable style preset.
Choose the Image profile, model or workflow and only the operations that its discovered capabilities support.
Run generation explicitly, compare results and accept the chosen image into managed project assets.
Use Avatar Gallery or Generate Expression Set for Front Porch alternate looks and expressions.
notes: Browsing results, editing presets and composing prompts do not call an Image provider.
Reference, Image-to-Image and Inpainting inputs are explicit and never inferred from unrelated Vision attachments.

articles.title: Export a character
articles.summary: Preview the target format and artwork before writing a card.
steps: Open Export or Install from a saved Workspace project.
Choose the target export profile and inspect the exact mapped, preserved, transformed and omitted fields.
Resolve the unfinished-character safety check if all core roleplay fields are empty.
Choose artwork for PNG output, or explicitly confirm a definition-only export when supported.
Select a destination and complete the local export.
notes: Character Card Forge warns about missing artwork because a successful JSON definition can otherwise look like a failed PNG export.

articles.title: Connect and install to Front Porch
articles.summary: Use supported APIs and portable formats without direct database writes.
steps: Open Export or Install and configure the Front Porch address for the current session.
Run Connection Diagnostics to verify reachability, authentication and supported endpoints.
Sign in when required; passwords, two-factor codes and cookies are not persisted.
Preview collisions and remote differences before Create Copy, Update or Replace actions.
Use supported APIs or portable files for characters, groups, worlds, galleries and chats.
notes: Character Card Forge never reads or writes the Front Porch SQLite database.
Optional Front Porch character-life fields do not enter ordinary cards unless the target format carries that extension.

articles.title: Back up and recover work
articles.summary: Protect projects, revisions and portable libraries before risky changes.
steps: Keep backups of the active Character Card Forge library or portable library folder while the app is closed.
Use Revision History checkpoints for field-level comparison, selective recovery, restore or fork.
Use Archive for recoverable Library removal and project packages for portable project copies.
If a portable share is unavailable, reconnect it and reopen the project from that library; do not create a substitute path.
Resolve external-change conflicts by reviewing both copies instead of overwriting blindly.
notes: Portable/shared folders are single-writer. Close the project on one computer before editing it on another.

articles.title: Troubleshoot a problem
articles.summary: Capture the narrowest useful evidence without exposing private content.
steps: Repeat the smallest action that shows the problem and record what you expected and what happened.
For generation failures, open that job's Generation Diagnostics and review the credential-redacted request summary.
For Front Porch problems, run Connection Diagnostics and note which supported capability failed.
Open Support & Diagnostics for the app/environment summary; model identifiers remain optional.
Create a bug report with reproducible steps, the app version and only the diagnostic files you reviewed.
notes: Never post API keys, passwords, cookies, private character text or private chat transcripts in a public issue.

articles.title: Diagnostics and privacy
articles.summary: Understand what the general support report includes and excludes.
steps: Open Support & Diagnostics and read the complete report preview.
Leave model identifiers disabled unless the provider/model is relevant to the problem.
Copy or export the report only after reviewing it.
Use Open Bug Report only when ready; the app never submits the report automatically.
notes: The general report always omits character/project content, prompts, conversations, credentials, sessions, endpoint addresses, custom profile names and file paths.
